messages:
oliver: Quick data point: ran an nsys capture against the KV-batched emission path. saw a ~900ms blank on the GPU timeline during steady token emit window. Capture used short duration to keep file size down.

jin: Can you paste the exact CLI you used? want to reproduce on the perf rig.

oliver: `nsys profile --output=kv_mini --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none --duration=8s --capture-range=auto ./bench_infer.sh` — focused on the hot slice. CPU threads show continuous scheduling but GPU timeline has a long empty span.

maya: `--sample=none` disables periodic sampling so you only rely on NVTX/OSRT markers. our batching fan-out frequently enqueues tiny eviction kernels on a helper stream w/out NVTX, so capture-range=auto can miss them. Try `--sample=periodic --sample-interval=100us` and `--capture-range=cudaProfilerApi`.

carla: Agree. Also add explicit NVTX around the worker threads that enqueue eviction/fanout. `capture-range=auto` sometimes anchors to the wrong host thread and drops cross-thread kernels.

oliver: Good tips. I did want OSRT markers to see the host->device handoff, hence `trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt`. Is there any additional flags to force inclusion of async streams?

jin: The usual repro we run for mixed async workloads is: `nsys profile --output=kv_full --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sample=periodic --sample-interval=200us --duration=22s ./bench_infer.sh`. Use `nvtxRangePushA("req-<id>")/nvtxRangePop()` in the runtime around per-request flow and call `cudaProfilerStart/Stop` implicitly via the capture range.

maya: Also set `NSYS_MONITOR=1` and `NSYS_DEBUG=1` in the env. nsys will print logs that indicate if OSRT brackets were created and if any streams were skipped or assigned to a different host thread. That debug log helped us catch a case where a heartbeat landed between NVTX pushes.

carla: If you're worried about qdrep size, do several short captures with different capture-range modes and compare timelines. often the missing activity appears in the cudaProfilerApi capture but not in auto.

oliver: Re-ran on the perf box with your command and NVTX in the eviction path. timeline snippet below (simplified):

--- timeline ---
cpu nvtx:batch_start 0.00s -> nvtx:batch_end 0.14s
gpu kernel decode 0.01s -> 0.03s
gpu kernel kv_lookup 0.05s -> 0.06s
gpu <blank> 0.06s -> 0.96s   <-- long hole
gpu kernel emit 0.96s -> 0.99s
-----------------

NVTXs show ranges for batch_start/end and we annotated eviction thread too, but the gap still existed.

jin: Does `NSYS_DEBUG` report any excluded streams or OSRT mismatch lines? Also run with `--sample-interval=50us` once; short microkernels can be missed by coarse sampling.

oliver: When I dropped to 50us the eviction microkernels showed up and the blank shrank to ~80ms. It seems the workload has many ~5-10us kernels that are frequent; with large sample intervals they can average out to a blank.

maya: That matches past behavior: many tiny, high-frequency kernels can disappear for `--sample=periodic` if interval > kernel duration. For debug runs we pick 20-50us. For full profiling keep 100-200us to limit file size.

carla: If OSRT brackets still misalign, add a per-request NVTX id that you push in all threads that touch the request (scheduler thread, worker threads enqueuing kernels). That makes correlation easier even if the profiler assigns OSRT bracket to one host thread.

perf-bot: note: qdrep can grow large. use `nsys stats --report=summary --report=timeline kv_full.qdrep` to get hotspot tables and `nsys export --output=summary.csv kv_full.qdrep` for a compact CSV.

oliver: Plan: 1) add NVTX to eviction threads 2) run `nsys profile --output=kv_diag --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sample=periodic --sample-interval=50us --duration=30s` 3) set NSYS_DEBUG=1 4) collect qdrep and run `nsys stats --report=summary` and `--report=activity`. will paste summary and stack traces next.

maya: If you want, I can run a trimmed variant on the other perf machine (different driver) to rule out driver scheduling differences.

oliver: appreciate it. thanks all — will upload the summary and tiny qdrep excerpt.
